question: Should OpenClaw add a parallel operator-installed internal `session:end` contract, or explicitly standardize typed plugin lifecycle hooks as the supported workflow-completion integration surface?
rationale: Source establishes the missing internal event and the existing plugin alternatives, but only maintainers can define the intended lifecycle semantics and decide whether maintaining two overlapping public hook systems is desirable.

options.title: Standardize Plugin Hooks
options.body: Document `agent_end`, `subagent_ended`, and `session_end` as the supported orchestration lifecycle and implement the Temporal signaling behavior as a ClawHub plugin.

options.title: Define Internal Session End
options.body: Specify one precise internal event payload and an emission matrix covering gateway, cron, subagent, reset, error, cancellation, and shutdown paths before implementation.

recommendation.title: Standardize Plugin Hooks
recommendation.body: Document `agent_end`, `subagent_ended`, and `session_end` as the supported orchestration lifecycle and implement the Temporal signaling behavior as a ClawHub plugin.

likelyOwner.reason: The available history and linked discussion most directly associate this person with the plugin and hook contract boundary requiring the decision.
